subject: Tri-Geo surge gateway pool proposal and handoff
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro: Surge Gateway tri-geo pilot - capacity ask (APAC lead)

Team,

Quick summary from this morning's call with Surge Gateway (Eva + Michael): they're moving a beta of their live inference proxy into APAC in mid-May and want a tri-geo dedicated footprint (APAC primary, EU and US as failover/burst). Key asks in the attached spreadsheet, but high-level:

- Pilot start: target week of 2027-05-15
- Initial steady-state target (APAC): 12 H100-equivalent GPUs (single-tenant pool) with burst lanes to 20 for peak windows
- EU & US: warm standby pools (5 H100s each) with cross-region fallback routing
- Expected QPS: 250 sustained across APAC during business hours; peaks up to 1,100 QPS for short bursts (15–45m) during product events
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for 512-token responses (model family: Llama-3 70B / quantized FP16 ribbon recommended)
- Token profile: average 280 tokens per request; cost sensitivity — they asked for batching + KV cache enabled to shave per-token costs

Provisional timeline: procurement wants committed capacity by 2027-04-22 to align purchase cycles. Eva attached their traffic sample and requested a quoted SOW.

Asks:
1) David - can infra validate the APAC 12->20 burst plan (H100-equivalent) and give node count + expected utilization for the first 90 days? Include autoscale cushion and warm standby bandwidth.
2) Karthik - procurement/pricing: what reserve/commit options should we offer to make this viable for both sides?
3) Lauren - can you draft a short runbook (canary, rollout, rollback) for the pilot with model pin + fallback rules so we can include it in the SOW?

Attachments: [Attachment: surge_gateway_capacity_request_v1.xlsx] [Attachment: proposal_runbook_draft.pdf]

Thanks — heading into the follow-up call tomorrow with their engineering lead.

– Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Surge Gateway tri-geo pilot - capacity ask (APAC lead)

Thanks Soojin — recapping infra's read after an initial capacity sketch.

Notes / assumptions:
- "H100-equivalent" mapped to our serving units: 1 H100 = ~1 serving unit for large LLMs; for quantized Llama-3 70B we estimate 1 GPU can sustain ~60–80 concurrent low-latency streams (512 tokens) depending on batching.
- For APAC steady 250 QPS with avg 280 tokens, we model (conservative) 1.2k tokens/sec sustained. With batching and KV caching, effective token throughput improves ~1.6x.

Preliminary recommendation (config + margins):
- APAC primary pool: 12 H100s reserved + 8 burst nodes (total 20) — same as ask. This yields headroom for 6–8x baseline business-hours growth for the 90-day pilot.
- EU / US warm standby: 6 H100s each (slightly higher than their ask) to absorb regional failover and allow per-region SPOF testing.
- Autoscale policy: keep target utilization 55–65% (token latency headroom), scale steps of 2 nodes, cold-start buffer of 3 nodes for APAC to avoid latency spikes at day-start.
- Network: ensure cross-region peering for KV cache replication; estimate additional 5–7 Gbps sustained inter-region for peak syncs.

Open items we need from the customer to firm numbers:
- Traffic distribution by hour in APAC (CSV) — we saw the sample but need a 14-day sample with peaks annotated.
- Confirmation of model family + whether they want warm cache snapshots replicated to EU/US (adds storage + egress).

Risk notes:
- If they use multi-threaded client bursts (short high-concurrency spikes) we must add 10–15% more headroom beyond burst nodes.
- If they request encrypted KV cache replication (customer-managed keys), that may add ~10% CPU overhead on control plane nodes.

I can produce a sizing spreadsheet with node-level ETA and cost delta by EOD Friday if that helps.

– David
David Kim
Principal Infra Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Surge Gateway tri-geo pilot - capacity ask (APAC lead)

Looping procurement and pricing guidance.

Options to present to Surge Gateway:
1) Pilot reserve (short-term): 3-month reserved APAC pool (12 nodes) + on-demand burst to 20. Discount: 12% off list for the 3-month commit.
2) Annual commitment: 12-month reserved APAC (10 nodes committed) + 12 additional committed nodes split across EU/US as part of a tri-geo package. Discount: 25% with added SLA credits.
3) Hybrid: reserved baseline + committed burst credits (a bucket of node-hours they can draw from for product events) — attractive for customers with spiky event-based traffic.

Procurement notes:
- Lead time: H100 procurement for dedicated pools typically 6–9 weeks from order to live in APAC region for private racks; if hosted we can onboard faster (2–3 weeks) leveraging cloud partners but cost delta ~+18%.
- Legal wants a clarified data residency clause if we replicate KV snapshots to EU/US. Suggest: store customer keys in KMS; snapshots transit encrypted; retention policy 30 days default unless they request longer.

Pricing ask: Soojin, can you confirm which commercial path they prefer (hosted vs dedicated on-prem racks)? That will materially change the numbers and the procurement ETA. Also, for deal packaging, recommend we tie the pilot to a mutual action plan (MAP) with 3 milestones: pilot activation, load test, production handoff.

– Karthik
Head of Procurement & GTM Ops

From: Michael Turner <m.turner@edgegrid.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Eva Nakamura <eva@surge-gateway.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tri-Geo surge gateway pool proposal and handoff

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 15:02 PDT, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — can you confirm whether hosted or dedicated makes more sense for timing/cost?

We (Surge Gateway / EdgeGrid engineering) are fine with either but prioritize time-to-live and a simple SOW for the pilot. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We can accept hosted in APAC for the initial 90-day pilot if that gets us live by mid-May; dedicated racks are preferred long-term but may push activation out.
- Traffic sample: uploading 14-day window now to the Drive folder. Expect a concentrated spike pattern tied to two weekly product demos — each spike is ~8–12x baseline for 20–30 minutes.
- Model confirmation: we'll start with Llama-3 70B quantized FP16; if performance ok we may move to a trimmed 33B family for cost optimization.
- KV cache replication: prefer async replication to EU/US; encrypted in flight, keys in our KMS (we can provide access controls).

Next steps: please send a short SOW that covers pilot duration, committed nodes, burst credits, rollback conditions, and a runbook for failure scenarios. We need an internal approval note by 2027-04-22.

Thanks — Michael
Michael Turner
VP Engineering (Surge Gateway / EdgeGrid)
[Attachment referenced: surge_gateway_capacity_request_v1.xlsx]
